en: The *Sutra Spoken by the Buddha on the Mātaṅga Woman Resolving Six Matters within the Body*, translated anonymously and appended to the Eastern Jin records.
The Buddha was staying at the Anāthapiṇḍada Ārāma in Śrāvastī. At that time, Ānanda was walking about with his alms bowl.
While begging for alms, Ānanda followed the course of a stream and saw a woman carrying water away from the bank; he asked her for some water, and the woman gave it to him.
The girl followed Ānanda to his dwelling place.
Upon her return home, she told her mother—whose name was Mātaṅgī—that she had been left lying in the house and weeping. Her mother asked her, "Why are you weeping?"
The girl said, "Mother, if you wish to marry me off, do not give me to another.
By the water's edge, I saw a śramaṇa who begged me for water; when I questioned him, his name was Ānanda."
"I shall marry only if I obtain Ānanda; if I do not obtain Ānanda, I will not marry.
Her mother then went to inquire after Ānanda, for Ānanda was serving the Buddha.
The mother immediately learned of this and returned to tell her daughter:
"Ānanda serves the Buddha’s Way; he is unwilling to be your husband.
The daughter then wept and refused to eat.
"The mother knows the way of sorcery; why do you not guide her?
The mother went out to invite Ānanda to return for a meal, and the daughter was greatly delighted.
The mother said to Ānanda:
"I wish to give my daughter to you as a wife. Ānanda said,
"I uphold the Buddha's precepts and am not permitted to keep a wife."
The mother spoke again:
"If my daughter does not obtain you as her husband, she will commit suicide.
Ānanda said:
"I serve as a disciple of the Buddha; I may not engage in sexual relations with women.
His mother then entered and said to her daughter, "Ānanda is unwilling to be your husband. Those who possess the Way and its scriptures are not permitted to keep wives."
The daughter replied to her mother while weeping,
"Where does the path of a mother lead?
Her mother said:
"In all the paths under heaven, none can surpass the path of the Buddha and that of the Arhat.
The woman spoke again:
"Just close the doors for me so that no one may leave; when evening comes, you shall become my husband."
The mother immediately closed the door and bound Ānanda with sorcery.

When the time of the afternoon meal arrived, the mother prepared a mat for him to lie upon. The daughter was greatly delighted and adorned herself; however, Ānanda refused to go to the place where he was to lie down. The mother then lit a fire and, stepping forward, pulled at Ānanda’s robe and said to him:
"If you do not become my daughter's husband, I shall throw you into the fire."
Ānanda, feeling self-contempt for his life as a śramaṇa, thought, "Today I am instead trapped within and cannot escape," whereupon he joined his palms and called out to the Buddha.
The Buddha immediately knew this and sent a divine being to release Ānanda.
Ānanda went to where the Buddha was and said, "Yesterday, while walking for alms, I saw a woman by the water's edge and asked her for some water.
Tomorrow, a man named Mātaṅga invited me to his home for a meal; as soon as I stepped out, he grabbed me, wishing to give his daughter to me to be my wife."
"I uphold the Buddha's precepts and may not keep a wife.
When the woman saw that Ānanda had escaped and departed, she wept at home;
her mother said, "As for those who serve the Buddha, my path cannot surpass theirs. Did I not tell you so from the beginning?"
The girl did not stop weeping and continued to think of Ānanda.
On the following day, she went in person to seek out Ānanda; seeing him again as he was walking for alms, she followed behind him, gazing at his feet and looking up at his face.
Ānanda felt ashamed; he lowered his head, would not look at her, and tried to avoid her, but the woman continued to follow him without ceasing.
Ānanda returned to the Buddha’s dwelling, yet the woman remained guarding the gate. When Ānanda would not come out, the woman wept and departed.
Ānanda came forward and said to the Buddha,
“The woman Mātaṅgī follows today and will come again tomorrow.
The Buddha then called for the woman to be brought before him.
The Buddha said, “You have gone after Ānanda; what do you seek?
The woman replied:
“I have heard that Ānanda has no wife, and I likewise have no husband; I wish to become Ānanda’s wife.
The Buddha said, “Ānanda the śramaṇa is hairless; would you be willing to shave off your hair?”
"I shall send Ānanda to serve as your husband.
The woman said,
"I dare not shave my hair."
The Buddha said,
"Go back and inform your mother that you have come after having your head shaved.
The daughter returned to her mother's place and said:
"My mother could not bring Ānanda; I have come myself to inquire after the Buddha.
The Buddha said:
'If you shave your hair and come to me, I shall cause Ānanda to become your husband.'"
The mother said, "I have raised you with the care of protecting your hair; why do you wish to become the wife of a śramaṇa?
There are great and wealthy men in the kingdom; I myself can marry you to one of them."
The girl said,
"When I die and am reborn, I shall become the wife of Ānanda.
Her mother said:
"Why do you bring disgrace upon your own lineage?
The girl said,
"If my mother loves me, she should follow whatever my heart desires."
The mother immediately shed tears and took up the razor to shave her daughter's hair.
The daughter returned to where the Buddha was and said,
"I have already shaved my hair."
The Buddha asked,
"What is it that you love about Ānanda?
The woman replied:
"I love Ānanda’s eyes; I love Ānanda’s nose; I love Ānanda’s mouth; I love Ānanda’s voice; I love Ānanda’s gait. The Buddha said:
"In the eyes there are tears; in the nose there is mucus; in the mouth there is saliva; in the ears there is wax; in the body there are excrement and urine—all of which are foul places."

Those who become husband and wife then fall into states of suffering; within those states they give birth to children; having children, there is death; and with death comes weeping and wailing. What benefit is there for the self in all this?

The woman then reflected within herself; amidst the impurities of her physical form, she attained a state of right mind and thereby realized the path of Arhatship. Having attained Arhatship, she was established therein.
The Buddha said to the woman,
"Rise and go to where Ānanda is.
The woman, feeling ashamed, lowered her head and knelt before the Buddha, saying:
"Truly, it was because of my ignorance that I pursued Ānanda; now my mind has been opened, like a lamp lit in the darkness;
like one who, while on a boat, reaches the shore when the vessel breaks;
like a blind man who finds a guide."
"The old man was able to walk by holding a staff; now the Buddha has shown me the Way, and my mind has opened up in this way.
All the śramaṇas together asked the Buddha, "This woman's mother practiced sorcery; by what cause did she attain the path of an arhat?"
The Buddha asked,
"Do you śramaṇas wish to hear and know about this woman?
The śramaṇas replied:
"We shall receive your instruction.
The Buddha said,
"This woman of the Mātaṅga clan was, in former times for five hundred lifetimes, the wife of Ānanda."

For five hundred lifetimes, they have respected and cherished one another, and now, together within the path of the sutras and precepts, they have attained the Way. Now, though husband and wife, they look upon each other as brothers; this sutra causes all śramaṇas to know that such is the nature of a woman’s mind.
The śramaṇas then rose and prostrated themselves before the Buddha.
[End of] the *Mātaṅgī-parivrājikā-ṣaḍvastu-vinirmukti-sūtra*.
